title: Bodies of civilians found in Bucha and Irpin after Russian withdrawal
body:
Reports and images of killed civilians emerged from Bucha and Irpin, towns northwest of Kyiv, in early April 2022 after Russian forces withdrew from the area. Ukrainian forces retook Irpin on 28 March and Bucha on 1 April. On 2 April, Ukraine said that Kyiv Oblast was free of Russian forces. Before the war Irpin had about 60,000 residents and Bucha about 28,000. Bucha had spent weeks under Russian control, and Irpin had been partly controlled by Russian forces.

Photos and videos published by the Kyiv Independent on 3 April showed ruined houses, burned cars and civilian bodies on the streets. Many bodies in Bucha had their hands tied behind their backs, which the outlet said pointed to organised killing. Men were often found shot dead. Bucha mayor Anatoly Fedoruk said that authorities had collected 280 bodies in the first day after the town's liberation and buried them in mass graves. The State Emergency Service reported that it found and deactivated 643 explosives in Irpin on 2 April alone.

Russian authorities denied targeting civilians. The discovery of the bodies prompted international condemnation and calls for investigations into war crimes. The UN human rights office later sent officers to Bucha, and on 22 April 2022 UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet said they had documented the unlawful killing of about 50 civilians in the town.
